osmos — the gradual movement of a system toward a shared equilibrium.

Version control for the way you actually work.

Osmos is a local-first version control system built for designers, writers, and teams. No cloud required. No complex CLI commands. Just your files, versioned and synced across your devices — privately, locally, and fast.

§1 — Principles

Version control for everyone.

01 Versioning

Snapshot-based

Every save is a full snapshot, not a complex diff. Revert a single file or an entire commit instantly with two-level rollback. Conflicts are automatically resolved by timestamp (LWW) via the central hub.

02 Networking

Local & Offline

Work without a connection and sync when ready. Osmos uses mDNS to discover devices on your local network. Once reachable, your local queue syncs with the hub instantly. Completely offline-capable.

03 Security

End-to-end encrypted

Your files are encrypted with PBKDF2-derived keys that only you hold. Data is stored securely via AES-GCM and transport is protected via the Noise Protocol. Total privacy by design.

§2 — Specification

Technical overview.

Interface
SwiftUI, MD3, Native · No CLI required
Architecture
Hub & Client · local-first, peer-to-peer
Versioning
Snapshots · two-level rollback
Conflict resolution
Timestamp (LWW) · admin queue for pending changes
Discovery
mDNS (_osmos._tcp.local) · on the local subnet
Encryption
AES-GCM via CryptoKit · Noise Protocol for transport
Recovery
BIP-39 · 24-word recovery phrase
Core Engine
Rust · with optional gitoxide backend
Platform
Apple, Android, Windows, Linux · Cross-platform native
Status
v0.1.0-α · In active development
§3 — Roadmap

What's next for Osmos.

Phase 1 Current

Core & macOS Alpha

Stabilizing the Rust engine, mDNS peer discovery, and LWW conflict resolution. Releasing the initial Hub & Client native interface for macOS built with SwiftUI.

Phase 2 In Development

Cross-Platform Beta

Expanding client support with Material Design 3 for Android, and native UIs for Windows and Linux. Rolling out iOS read-only companion app and robust FFI bindings.

Phase 3 Planned

Git Interop & v1.0

Integrating the optional gitoxide backend for seamless import/export to legacy Git repositories. Finalizing admin queue workflows and security audits for the 1.0 release.
